exampleSentence: Active health checks remove dead backends within seconds.
exampleSentences: Active health checks remove dead backends within seconds.
Our active health check uses a shallow endpoint instead of the real one.
Without active health checks the balancer keeps sending traffic to a crashed pod.
We made the active health check interval longer to reduce probe load.

defCn: 被动健康检查：依据真实业务请求的成败来推断后端健康状态。
defEn: A scheme that infers backend health from the outcome of real user requests.
exampleSentence: Passive health check caught the degraded backend that answered with empty results.
exampleSentences: Passive health check caught the degraded backend that answered with empty results.
Passive health check is more accurate but it only reacts to real traffic.
Combine passive health check with active probes for faster detection.
The passive check recorded failures and ejected the node after five errors.

defCn: 慢启动：新节点上线后逐步提升其承接流量比例，避免瞬时压垮。
defEn: The gradual ramp-up of traffic sent to a newly added backend.
exampleSentence: Slow start keeps a freshly started pod from drowning under the first wave of requests.
exampleSentences: Slow start keeps a freshly started pod from drowning under the first wave of requests.
Without slow start, every deploy causes a brief but real latency spike.
The slow start window should match the time the app needs to warm its caches.
We extended the slow start period for the recommendation service.

defCn: 连接排空：下线节点前停止接收新请求并等待存量连接自然结束。
defEn: The process of stopping new traffic and letting existing connections finish before shutdown.
exampleSentence: Connection draining prevented the deploy from cutting user sessions in half.
exampleSentences: Connection draining prevented the deploy from cutting user sessions in half.
Graceful shutdown with connection draining avoids five hundred client errors.
Our connection draining window is shorter than the longest websocket session.
Without connection draining, deploys always produced a burst of retries.

defCn: 健康路由：仅把流量转发到当前判定为健康的实例上。
defEn: Routing that only sends traffic to instances that currently pass health checks.
exampleSentence: Health-based routing kept half of the fleet serving users during the bad deployment.
exampleSentences: Health-based routing kept half of the fleet serving users during the bad deployment.
Health-based routing turns a partial outage into a partial slowdown.
We combined health-based routing with a circuit breaker per dependency.
The mesh applies health-based routing automatically for every outbound call.

defCn: 离群检测：识别出与群体表现显著不同的实例并将其排除。
defEn: The identification of instances whose behaviour deviates sharply from their peers.
codeExample:
z = (latency - mean) / stddev
if z > 3: flag_outlier(instance)
exampleSentence: Outlier detection ejected the machine with a failing disk before it slowed the cluster.
exampleSentences: Outlier detection ejected the machine with a failing disk before it slowed the cluster.
Outlier detection uses latency and error rate to spot a sick node.
Without outlier detection a single slow machine ruins the p99 for everyone.
The scheduler performs outlier detection before assigning new work.

defCn: 负载均衡成员：注册到均衡器上的一个可被调度的后端实例。
defEn: A backend instance registered with the balancer and eligible for traffic.
exampleSentence: The balancer removed a member from rotation during the maintenance window.
exampleSentences: The balancer removed a member from rotation during the maintenance window.
Each balancer member reports its own connection count to the controller.
We drained every balancer member before the kernel upgrade.
A member returns to rotation once it passes two successful health checks.

defCn: 上游：请求流转方向上的调用方（代理视角的客户端一侧）。
defEn: The caller side of a connection, from the point of view of the server handling it.
exampleSentence: The proxy retries the upstream once before returning a bad gateway.
exampleSentences: The proxy retries the upstream once before returning a bad gateway.
Upstream timeouts are usually caused by the client cancelling the request.
We log the upstream host and status for every outbound call.
The gateway rate limits per upstream rather than per client.

defCn: 下游：被调用方，即请求实际到达并执行的服务。
defEn: The callee side of a call, the service that actually performs the work.
exampleSentence: The circuit breaker opened because the downstream service returned timeouts.
exampleSentences: The circuit breaker opened because the downstream service returned timeouts.
A slow downstream dependency turned into slow responses upstream.
We measure downstream latency separately for each dependency.
Retries only help when the downstream error is safe to repeat.

defCn: 四层负载均衡：在传输层按 IP 与端口转发流量，不解析应用内容。
defEn: Load balancing at the transport layer that forwards traffic by IP and port only.
codeExample:
listen 443
  mode tcp
  balance least_conn
  server app1 10.0.0.1:8443
exampleSentence: Layer four load balancing is faster but it cannot route by URL path.
exampleSentences: Layer four load balancing is faster but it cannot route by URL path.
Layer four load balancing preserves the client IP address without extra headers.
We use layer four load balancing for the database traffic that must keep TLS.
Switching from layer seven to layer four removed a hop from the request path.

defCn: 七层负载均衡：在应用层理解 HTTP 协议，可按路径、头部路由。
defEn: Application-layer load balancing that understands HTTP and routes by path or header.
exampleSentence: Layer seven load balancing let us send checkout traffic to a bigger cluster.
exampleSentences: Layer seven load balancing let us send checkout traffic to a bigger cluster.
Layer seven load balancing costs a bit more CPU but gives fine grained routing.
Our gateway uses layer seven load balancing to split canary and stable traffic.
Health checks for layer seven load balancing must hit a real HTTP endpoint.

defCn: 任播：同一 IP 由多个节点宣告，流量被路由到最近的一个。
defEn: A routing model where many nodes advertise the same address and traffic goes to the nearest one.
codeExample: anycast_ip = 203.0.113.10   # advertised by every edge node
exampleSentence: Anycast gives us a single global endpoint without writing our own geo router.
exampleSentences: Anycast gives us a single global endpoint without writing our own geo router.
Anycast hides node failures because the address simply advertises elsewhere.
The DNS provider supports anycast for our public resolvers.
Anycast cannot be used when the service must keep session state locally.

defCn: 全局负载均衡：跨地域把用户流量分派到最合适的可用区或集群。
defEn: Routing users across regions to the best available data centre for each request.
exampleSentence: Global server load balancing kept European users on local storage during the outage.
exampleSentences: Global server load balancing kept European users on local storage during the outage.
Global server load balancing weighs latency, cost and regional health.
We added global server load balancing to avoid a single region becoming a bottleneck.
The policy is defined per hostname so internal traffic skips it entirely.

defCn: 流量引导：按权重或规则把部分流量导向特定服务版本或区域。
defEn: Directing a configurable share of traffic toward a particular version or region.
exampleSentence: Traffic steering let us ship the new ranking model to one percent of users first.
exampleSentences: Traffic steering let us ship the new ranking model to one percent of users first.
We use traffic steering to compare two model versions on live traffic.
Traffic steering rules changed in under a minute during the incident.
The steering config is versioned and reviewed like any other code.

defCn: 虚拟节点：一致性哈希中为每个物理节点分配的多个哈希占位点。
defEn: Multiple hash points assigned to one physical node to smooth key distribution.
codeExample: for i in range(vnode_count): ring[(hash(node.id) + i * 1) % RING] = node
exampleSentence: Three hundred virtual nodes keep the load evenly spread across eight machines.
exampleSentences: Three hundred virtual nodes keep the load evenly spread across eight machines.
Adding virtual nodes reduced the variance in bucket sizes per server.
Virtual nodes also make rebalancing cheaper when a node joins the ring.
The virtual node count is a tuning knob that trades memory for balance.

defCn: 哈希环：一致性哈希使用的环形空间，键与节点都映射其上。
defEn: The circular space used by consistent hashing where both keys and nodes are placed.
exampleSentence: The hash ring makes node removal move only a small slice of keys.
exampleSentences: The hash ring makes node removal move only a small slice of keys.
Walking the hash ring clockwise gives the owner of each key.
The hash ring is rebalanced automatically when a new node joins.
Virtual nodes thicken the hash ring and smooth the ownership distribution.

defCn: 再均衡：在节点增减后重新分配数据与负载，使各节点负载均衡。
defEn: Redistributing data and load across nodes after capacity or membership changes.
exampleSentence: Rebalancing ran overnight so the new storage nodes could catch up.
exampleSentences: Rebalancing ran overnight so the new storage nodes could catch up.
Rebalancing is expensive, so we schedule it when traffic is low.
The cluster rebalances automatically once a node is marked out of service.
A slow rebalance left two shards hot for nearly an hour.

defCn: 热点分区：承载远超其他分区访问量或写入量的那一块数据。
defEn: A single partition that receives far more traffic or writes than the others.
exampleSentence: One celebrity account created a hot partition that saturated the whole broker.
exampleSentences: One celebrity account created a hot partition that saturated the whole broker.
A hot partition is usually caused by a poor shard key choice.
We split the hot partition into eight smaller ranges to spread the load.
The dashboard flags a hot partition before the consumer lag explodes.

defCn: 分散聚合：向多个分片并行发起查询再汇总结果的一种访问模式。
defEn: A query pattern that fans requests out to many shards and merges the answers.
codeExample:
results = await Promise.all(shards.map(s => s.search(q)))
return merge(results)
exampleSentence: Scatter-gather queries fan out to every shard, so the slowest shard sets the latency.
exampleSentences: Scatter-gather queries fan out to every shard, so the slowest shard sets the latency.
Scatter-gather works well for aggregations that tolerate partial results.
A scatter-gather query over a thousand shards created a fan-out storm.
We cache scatter-gather results because the fan-out is expensive.

defCn: 直写缓存：写请求同时更新缓存与持久化存储，保证缓存不会落后。
defEn: A caching strategy that writes to the cache and the backing store together.
codeExample:
db.write(row)
cache.set(key, row)   # both updated before responding
exampleSentence: Write-through caching removes the risk of stale values after an update.
exampleSentences: Write-through caching removes the risk of stale values after an update.
Write-through is slower than write-back but much easier to reason about.
We use write-through for the price catalogue and write-back for counters.
The downside of write-through is added latency on every write path.

defCn: 回写缓存：先写缓存，延迟批量落盘，由后台线程持久化。
defEn: A caching strategy that updates the cache first and persists to storage asynchronously.
exampleSentence: Write-back caching keeps the write path fast but risks data loss on crash.
exampleSentences: Write-back caching keeps the write path fast but risks data loss on crash.
Write-back suits counter and metric workloads that tolerate small losses.
We moved from write-back to write-through after the incident review.
The flush interval decides how much data a crash can destroy.

defCn: 读穿缓存：缓存未命中时由缓存层负责回源读取并回填。
defEn: A caching strategy where the cache itself loads and stores missing entries.
exampleSentence: Read-through caching keeps the database call inside the cache layer.
exampleSentences: Read-through caching keeps the database call inside the cache layer.
Read-through avoids duplicating the fallback logic in every caller.
The read-through loader retries once before giving up on the origin.
Read-through pairs naturally with a single flight guard.

defCn: 缓存击穿：热点键过期瞬间大量请求同时回源压垮数据库。
defEn: A thundering herd of requests hitting the origin when a hot key expires.
codeExample:
lock = cache.lock(key, ttl=5)
if lock.acquire(): rebuild_cache()
exampleSentence: A cache stampede took the database down for ninety seconds on a single popular key.
exampleSentences: A cache stampede took the database down for ninety seconds on a single popular key.
We prevent a cache stampede with a single flight lock and stale-while-revalidate.
The stampede happened because thousands of instances refreshed the same key together.
Adding jitter to the TTL reduced the stampede risk as well.

defCn: 缓存穿透：查询本就不存在的数据，导致每次请求都回源。
defEn: Repeated lookups for keys that do not exist, so every request falls through to the origin.
codeExample: if not found: cache.set(key, NULL, ttl=60)   # negative caching
exampleSentence: Cache penetration from bot traffic was hammering the user profile table.
exampleSentences: Cache penetration from bot traffic was hammering the user profile table.
A bloom filter in front of the cache blocks most cache penetration attempts.
Negative caching is the standard defence against cache penetration.
The attacker's random identifiers caused constant cache penetration.

defCn: 缓存雪崩：大量键同时过期或缓存整体失效造成回源洪峰。
defEn: A wave of origin traffic caused by many keys expiring or the cache failing at once.
exampleSentence: A cache avalanche after the Redis restart overwhelmed the primary database.
exampleSentences: A cache avalanche after the Redis restart overwhelmed the primary database.
Randomised TTLs are the classic fix for a cache avalanche.
The cache avalanche took down checkout for four minutes last March.
We also keep a warm standby replica of the cache for this reason.

defCn: 缓存预取：预测即将访问的数据并提前加载进缓存。
defEn: Loading data into the cache before a request actually needs it.
codeExample:
on_list_response(ids):
  for id in ids: cache.prefetch('item:' + id)
exampleSentence: Cache prefetch on list endpoints made detail pages feel instant.
exampleSentences: Cache prefetch on list endpoints made detail pages feel instant.
Cache prefetch is cheap when the read pattern is predictable.
Aggressive cache prefetch wasted memory on data nobody opened.
We added cache prefetch after the list page became the main entry point.

defCn: 淘汰策略：缓存空间不足时决定移除哪些条目的规则。
defEn: The rule that decides which entries are removed when the cache runs out of space.
exampleSentence: Changing the eviction policy to LFU doubled the hit ratio for the image cache.
exampleSentences: Changing the eviction policy to LFU doubled the hit ratio for the image cache.
The eviction policy should match the access distribution of your data.
An LRU eviction policy works poorly for data with one hot key.
We tuned the eviction policy after the cache started thrashing.

defCn: 最不经常使用淘汰：移除访问次数最少的缓存条目。
defEn: Least frequently used, an eviction strategy that removes the least accessed entries.
exampleSentence: LFU kept the popular catalogue pages in memory under heavy churn.
exampleSentences: LFU kept the popular catalogue pages in memory under heavy churn.
LFU protects expensive objects that are requested constantly.
The downside of LFU is that yesterday's popularity can outlive its usefulness.
We combine LFU with a TTL so stale popularity cannot block fresh data.

defCn: 最近最少使用淘汰：移除最久未被访问的缓存条目。
defEn: Most recently used, an eviction strategy that discards the oldest entry first.
exampleSentence: MRU eviction suits a scan-heavy workload where recent data is about to be reused.
exampleSentences: MRU eviction suits a scan-heavy workload where recent data is about to be reused.
MRU is the opposite of LRU and is rarely the default for good reason.
For a sequential scan, MRU eviction protects the working set.
We tested MRU for the streaming buffer and hit more cache misses.

defCn: 生存时间：缓存条目在失效前允许保留的时长。
defEn: Time to live, the duration a cache entry stays valid before it expires.
exampleSentence: A short TTL keeps the catalogue fresh without hammering the database.
exampleSentences: A short TTL keeps the catalogue fresh without hammering the database.
The TTL of the session cache is fifteen minutes.
Randomising the TTL avoids mass expiration at the same second.
Longer TTLs mean better hit ratios but staler data.

defCn: 缓存命中率：请求直接由缓存满足的比例。
defEn: The proportion of lookups served directly from the cache.
exampleSentence: A cache hit ratio of ninety-five percent saves us four hundred database queries per second.
exampleSentences: A cache hit ratio of ninety-five percent saves us four hundred database queries per second.
We track the cache hit ratio per endpoint, not just in aggregate.
The hit ratio fell sharply when the schema changed and keys started missing.
Improving the hit ratio was cheaper than buying faster disks.

defCn: 负缓存：把「不存在」这一结果也缓存起来以阻断穿透。
defEn: Caching the fact that a key is absent so repeated misses do not reach the origin.
exampleSentence: Negative caching with a short TTL is the cheapest defence against cache penetration.
exampleSentences: Negative caching with a short TTL is the cheapest defence against cache penetration.
We cache misses for sixty seconds to stop the bot traffic.
Negative caching must be invalidated quickly when data is created.
A sentinel value distinguishes a negative cache hit from a real null.

defCn: 软过期：条目已标记过期但仍可在后台刷新期间被读取。
defEn: An entry that is logically expired but may still be served while it refreshes.
exampleSentence: Soft expiry keeps latency low while the background refresh brings the value up to date.
exampleSentences: Soft expiry keeps latency low while the background refresh brings the value up to date.
Serving soft expired data is acceptable for recommendation lists.
The soft expiry window should be much shorter than the hard one.
We alert only when the soft expiry backlog grows too large.

defCn: 硬过期：条目到期后必须重新加载，绝不返回旧值。
defEn: The point after which an entry must be reloaded and old values may not be served.
exampleSentence: Payment status uses a hard expiry because stale data would be dangerous.
exampleSentences: Payment status uses a hard expiry because stale data would be dangerous.
Hard expiry is required for security sensitive and financial data.
Our read-through cache distinguishes soft from hard expiry per record type.
Serving a hard expired value once is a correctness bug, not a performance issue.

defCn: 分层缓存：按访问速度把数据存放在内存、SSD 与磁盘等不同层级。
defEn: A cache that stores data across several media ordered by access speed.
exampleSentence: A tiered cache keeps hot data in memory and pushes cold data to disk.
exampleSentences: A tiered cache keeps hot data in memory and pushes cold data to disk.
The tiered cache cut our average read latency by two thirds.
A tiered cache is much cheaper than extending the fast tier to everything.
Promotion between tiers is triggered by the access frequency.

defCn: 进程内缓存：直接存放在应用进程内存中的本地缓存。
defEn: A cache that lives in the memory of the application process itself.
exampleSentence: An in-process cache removes network latency but is not shared between instances.
exampleSentences: An in-process cache removes network latency but is not shared between instances.
The in-process cache handles the repeated lookups of a single request.
An in-process cache is fast until the process restarts and loses everything.
We cap the in-process cache size to avoid out of memory errors.

defCn: 共享缓存：多个服务实例共同访问的集中式缓存。
defEn: A central cache that every application instance reads from and writes to.
exampleSentence: A shared cache is the only way to keep sessions valid across many pods.
exampleSentences: A shared cache is the only way to keep sessions valid across many pods.
The shared cache removes most of the traffic that used to hit the database.
A shared cache adds a network hop but saves a lot of repeated work.
We run the shared cache in a separate availability zone from the app tier.

defCn: Memcached：基于内存的分布式键值缓存服务。
defEn: A distributed in-memory key-value cache used to speed up dynamic sites.
exampleSentence: Memcached was the simplest way to add a shared cache to our stack.
exampleSentences: Memcached was the simplest way to add a shared cache to our stack.
We moved from Memcached to Redis when we needed persistence and pub-sub.
Memcached stores everything in memory, so a restart empties the cache.
The Memcached client hashes keys across servers to spread the load.

defCn: 准入策略：决定哪些新请求允许进入系统、由谁放行的规则。
defEn: The rule set that decides which incoming work is allowed into the system.
exampleSentence: A strict admission policy keeps the system usable when a dependency slows down.
exampleSentences: A strict admission policy keeps the system usable when a dependency slows down.
The admission policy rejects work once the queue exceeds its limit.
Our admission policy prioritises interactive traffic over batch jobs.
Changing the admission policy was faster than adding capacity.

defCn: 扫描抗性：缓存面对大量一次性访问时仍能保持高命中率的能力。
defEn: The ability of a cache to keep its hit rate high under a large scan of unique keys.
codeExample: if key not in bloom_filter: return miss   # rejects scans early
exampleSentence: A bloom filter gives the cache scan resistance against table dumps.
exampleSentences: A bloom filter gives the cache scan resistance against table dumps.
Scan resistance matters when attackers try to pull the whole dataset.
Without scan resistance, one report query can evict the whole cache.
The admission policy is also used to protect scan resistance.

defCn: 键规范化：把不同写法的请求键统一成同一个缓存键。
defEn: Converting differently spelled request keys into one canonical cache key.
exampleSentence: Key normalization doubled the hit ratio by merging trailing slash variants.
exampleSentences: Key normalization doubled the hit ratio by merging trailing slash variants.
Query strings often have to be stripped during key normalization.
Key normalization avoids duplicate cache entries for the same resource.
We documented the key normalization rules for every endpoint.

defCn: 工作集：当前活跃请求所真正需要访问的那部分数据。
defEn: The subset of data that active requests need at any moment.
exampleSentence: If the working set does not fit in memory, no cache policy can save you.
exampleSentences: If the working set does not fit in memory, no cache policy can save you.
The working set grew after we added the recommendation widget.
We sized the cache to hold the working set of a typical session.
Measuring the working set showed we needed twice the memory we had.

defCn: 请求放大：一次用户操作引发大量后端请求的现象。
defEn: The situation where one user action triggers many backend requests.
exampleSentence: A N plus one query is the classic example of request amplification.
exampleSentences: A N plus one query is the classic example of request amplification.
Request amplification made our page load cost more than the checkout.
We removed request amplification by batching the item lookups.
A CDN in front of the API also reduces request amplification.

defCn: 缓存亲和：让同一用户或实体的请求尽量落到同一缓存分片的机制。
defEn: Routing requests for the same user or entity to the same cache shard.
exampleSentence: Cache affinity keeps hot tenant data on one shard and preserves local hits.
exampleSentences: Cache affinity keeps hot tenant data on one shard and preserves local hits.
Without cache affinity, every request may touch a different shard.
Cache affinity is what makes the local hit rate acceptable.
We lost cache affinity when we introduced a random shard balancer.

defCn: 边缘缓存：把内容存放在靠近用户的 CDN 边缘节点上。
defEn: Storing content on CDN edge nodes close to the requesting user.
exampleSentence: Edge caching removed two thirds of the traffic that reached our origin.
exampleSentences: Edge caching removed two thirds of the traffic that reached our origin.
Edge caching helps most for static assets and public read APIs.
We enabled edge caching on the product page during the holiday campaign.
Edge caching works best when the cache key ignores personal data.

defCn: 边缘节点：部署在网络边缘、直接面向终端用户的服务器。
defEn: A server at the edge of the network that serves users directly.
codeExample:
edge_node = pop('LHR')
serve(asset)   # no origin round trip
exampleSentence: The nearest edge node serves the image in eight milliseconds.
exampleSentences: The nearest edge node serves the image in eight milliseconds.
Edge nodes cache popular objects and terminate the client connection.
A failed edge node is replaced by a new one within minutes.
Edge nodes make the origin invisible for most static requests.

defCn: 网络接入点：运营商在某个城市部署的边缘机房。
defEn: A physical location where a network operator hosts edge equipment.
exampleSentence: Adding a point of presence in Singapore cut latency for our Asian users.
exampleSentences: Adding a point of presence in Singapore cut latency for our Asian users.
The company operates twenty points of presence around the world.
A new point of presence halves the round trip time to the origin.
Traffic is routed to the closest point of presence with healthy capacity.

defCn: 源站：CDN 缓存未命中时真正提供原始内容的后端服务器。
defEn: The backend that holds the original content behind a CDN.
exampleSentence: The origin server must be able to absorb the full request volume.
exampleSentences: The origin server must be able to absorb the full request volume.
A cache miss falls through to the origin server.
We put a load balancer in front of the origin server for protection.
Origin server capacity matters most during a cold cache.

defCn: 源站防护层：位于边缘与源站之间的中间层，防止回源洪峰打垮源站。
defEn: An intermediate tier between edge nodes and the origin that absorbs origin traffic.
exampleSentence: The origin shield stopped a cache purge from becoming an outage.
exampleSentences: The origin shield stopped a cache purge from becoming an outage.
Without an origin shield, thousands of edges hit the origin at once.
The origin shield also absorbs traffic when a popular object expires.
We treat the origin shield as a tier of the cache hierarchy.

defCn: 缓存清除：主动让指定缓存内容失效以便发布新内容。
defEn: Actively invalidating specific cached content so fresh content can be served.
exampleSentence: A targeted cache purge is much safer than flushing the whole edge.
exampleSentences: A targeted cache purge is much safer than flushing the whole edge.
We run a cache purge right after the static bundle is deployed.
A full cache purge is expensive because every edge must refetch.
The release pipeline triggers the cache purge automatically.

defCn: 签名链接：带有效期与签名的临时访问地址。
defEn: A temporary access link carrying a signature and an expiry time.
exampleSentence: Signed URLs let us serve private video without exposing a public link.
exampleSentences: Signed URLs let us serve private video without exposing a public link.
The signed URL expires after ten minutes and then stops working.
We issue a signed URL only after checking the user's permission.
Never cache a signed URL at the edge because it will expire.

defCn: 防盗链：阻止第三方站点直接盗用本站静态资源的机制。
defEn: A mechanism that blocks other sites from hotlinking your static assets.
codeExample:
Referer-Policy: same-origin
if not allowed_referer(req.referer): return 403
exampleSentence: Hotlink protection cut our bandwidth bill after a popular blog copied our images.
exampleSentences: Hotlink protection cut our bandwidth bill after a popular blog copied our images.
Hotlink protection is often implemented as a referer allowlist.
We disabled hotlink protection for the embeddable widget on purpose.
Signed URLs are a stronger alternative to hotlink protection.

defCn: 边缘计算：在靠近用户的边缘节点上直接执行一部分业务逻辑。
defEn: Running part of the application logic on edge nodes near the user.

defCn: 全局限流：对所有实例统一计数的限流方式，避免总量失控。

defCn: 公平性：资源在所有用户或租户之间分配得均衡的程度。

defCn: 偏移量：消费者在分区日志中已处理到的位置编号。

defCn: 再平衡策略：决定如何把分区分配给组内成员的算法。

defCn: 粘性分配：再平衡时尽量保留成员原有分区的分配方式。

defCn: 组协调器：负责管理某个消费者组状态与分配的 broker 组件。

defCn: 领导者读取：只从分区领导者读取数据，以保证读到最新记录。

defCn: 跟随者读取：从副本读取数据以节省跨可用区带宽。

exampleSentences: Follower read cut our cross-zone bill but requires accepting stale data.

defCn: 副本因子：每个分区保存的副本数量。

exampleSentences: A replication factor of three survives the loss of two brokers.

defCn: 同步副本：已完全追上领导者日志、可参与选举的副本集合。

exampleSentence: When the in-sync replicas shrink to one, writes are blocked for safety.

defCn: 非清洁领导者选举：允许落后副本成为领导者以换取可用性。

exampleSentences: Unclean leader election keeps the service available but can lose records.

defCn: 生产者 ID：broker 为幂等生产者分配的唯一标识。

defCn: 事务型生产者：可把多条记录原子写入多个分区的生产者。
defEn: A producer that can atomically write records to multiple partitions.

producer.begin_transaction()

producer.send('b', v2)

exampleSentences: The transactional producer guarantees that both records appear or neither does.

defCn: 记录批次：一次写入中打包压缩的一组消息记录。
defEn: A group of message records packed and compressed into one write.

exampleSentences: Larger record batches improve throughput but add a little latency.

The producer compressed the record batch with the configured codec.

defCn: 确认超时：生产者等待 broker 确认写入的最长时间。

exampleSentences: A short acknowledgement timeout makes the producer fail fast on a stuck broker.

defCn: 消息确认：消费者向 broker 表明某条消息已被成功处理。

exampleSentences: Message acknowledgement is what advances the committed offset.

defCn: 负确认：消费者明确告知 broker 该消息处理失败需要重投。

exampleSentences: A negative acknowledgement sends the message to the retry path immediately.

defCn: 重投：消息在未被确认后被再次投递给消费者。

exampleSentences: Redelivery after a crash is the price of at-least-once delivery.

defCn: 投递次数：一条消息被投递给消费者并尝试处理的累计次数。

defCn: 投递保证：消息系统对消息不丢失、不重复所能提供的承诺级别。

defCn: 消息顺序：消息在分区内部按产生顺序被消费的保证。

defCn: 按键有序：保证同一业务键的消息按序处理，不同键之间不保证顺序。

defCn: 消息生存时间：消息在分区中保留的最长时长。

defCn: 倾斜分区：数据量或流量明显高于其他分区的那个分区。

defCn: 消息大小上限：单条消息允许占用的最大字节数。

defCn: 主题访问控制：针对具体主题授予或拒绝读写权限的规则。

exampleSentences: The topic ACL lets the analytics team read events without seeing the payment topic.

defCn: 消息转换：在写入或消费时对消息内容做格式改写。

defCn: 消息信封：包裹业务负载并附带元数据的外部结构。

defCn: 事件契约：对领域事件内容与触发语义的正式约定。
defEn: The formal agreement on the content and meaning of a domain event.
exampleSentence: The event contract states what happened, never who should act on it.
exampleSentences: The event contract states what happened, never who should act on it.
A good event contract mentions no downstream service.
We version the event contract whenever a field changes meaning.
Reviewing event contracts is how we avoid accidental coupling.

defCn: 模式注册中心：集中存放并校验消息结构定义的服务。
defEn: A central service that stores and validates the schema of messages.
codeExample:
schema = registry.get('order-value', version=3)
registry.register('order-value', avro_schema, version=4)
exampleSentence: The schema registry catches breaking changes before they reach production.
exampleSentences: The schema registry catches breaking changes before they reach production.
Our schema registry rejects a producer that sends an unknown field.
The schema registry is the single source of truth for event shapes.
Adding the schema registry to the pipeline cut production incidents.

defCn: 模式演进：在不破坏旧数据的前提下逐步修改消息结构的过程。
defEn: Changing a message schema over time while keeping old and new readers working.
exampleSentence: Schema evolution let us add a field without rewriting historical events.
exampleSentences: Schema evolution let us add a field without rewriting historical events.
Adding an optional field with a default is safe schema evolution.
The hard part of schema evolution is keeping old consumers alive.
We document the schema evolution rules for every event type.

defCn: 模式兼容性：新旧两版消息结构能否被同一消费者正确读取的属性。
defEn: Whether one version of a message schema can be read by a consumer written for another.
exampleSentence: The compatibility check runs in CI and blocks incompatible schema changes.
exampleSentences: The compatibility check runs in CI and blocks incompatible schema changes.
Backward compatibility means a new consumer can read old data.
Renaming a field is a backward incompatible change.
We enforce schema compatibility in the registry rather than by convention.

defCn: 契约兼容性：接口或事件约定变更后新旧双方仍能正常协作的能力。
defEn: The ability of producers and consumers to keep working after a contract change.
exampleSentence: Contract compatibility is the real constraint, not the elegance of the new format.
exampleSentences: Contract compatibility is the real constraint, not the elegance of the new format.
We test contract compatibility against every consumer before releasing.
A contract compatibility break means a coordinated deploy of both sides.
Versioning the contract is the usual way to preserve contract compatibility.

defCn: 路由键：消息上用于决定分发到哪个队列的标识。
defEn: The label on a message that determines which queue it is delivered to.
exampleSentence: The routing key decides where the message ends up in a topic exchange.
exampleSentences: The routing key decides where the message ends up in a topic exchange.
We use the aggregate id as the routing key so related events land together.
A wrong routing key means the message is silently discarded.
Wildcards in the binding let one queue match several routing keys.

defCn: 直连交换机：按路由键精确匹配绑定关系的交换机类型。
defEn: An exchange that delivers to queues whose binding key matches the routing key exactly.
exampleSentence: The direct exchange guarantees a message reaches only the intended queue.
exampleSentences: The direct exchange guarantees a message reaches only the intended queue.
We use a direct exchange when each event type has exactly one consumer.
A direct exchange is simpler to reason about than a fanout exchange.
The direct exchange also gives predictable routing for retry queues.

defCn: 扇出交换机：把消息复制到所有已绑定队列的交换机类型。
defEn: An exchange that copies every message to all of its bound queues.
exampleSentence: The fanout exchange is the simplest way to broadcast an event.
exampleSentences: The fanout exchange is the simplest way to broadcast an event.
The fanout exchange ignores the routing key entirely.
A fanout exchange is convenient but every subscriber pays the cost.
We replaced the fanout exchange with topic routing to reduce noise.

defCn: 绑定：交换机与队列之间建立 routing key 匹配关系的配置。
defEn: The configuration that links an exchange to a queue with a routing key pattern.
exampleSentence: A binding defines which queue receives the events of a given type.
exampleSentences: A binding defines which queue receives the events of a given type.
Adding a binding is how a new consumer starts receiving old and new events.
The binding pattern decides whether a subscriber sees every event.
We review the binding list whenever a new service subscribes.

defCn: 交换机：接收生产者消息并按规则路由到队列的中间组件。
defEn: An intermediary that receives messages from producers and routes them to queues.
exampleSentence: The exchange sits between the producer and the queue and decides the routing.
exampleSentences: The exchange sits between the producer and the queue and decides the routing.
A message published to an exchange with no binding is dropped.
We use one exchange per domain to keep routing rules readable.
The exchange also gives us a place to attach monitoring and quotas.

defCn: 消息总线：连接多个服务、让它们松耦合交换消息的中央通道。
defEn: A central channel that connects services so they can exchange messages loosely coupled.
exampleSentence: The message bus decouples the order service from every downstream consumer.
exampleSentences: The message bus decouples the order service from every downstream consumer.
A message bus becomes a bottleneck if every topic lives on one node.
We keep the message bus generic so producers never need to know consumers.
The team owns the message bus and publishes a catalogue of its topics.

defCn: 点对点消息：每条消息只被一个消费者处理的通信模型。
defEn: A messaging model where each message is handled by exactly one consumer.
exampleSentence: Point-to-point messaging fits work queues where each job has one owner.
exampleSentences: Point-to-point messaging fits work queues where each job has one owner.
Point-to-point messaging gives natural load balancing across workers.
We use point-to-point messaging for background job processing.
Switching to point-to-point messaging removed duplicate processing entirely.

defCn: 发布订阅模型：发布者不关心订阅者，消息广播给所有订阅方。
defEn: A model where publishers stay unaware of subscribers and messages are broadcast to all of them.
exampleSentence: The pub-sub model keeps producers completely independent of consumers.
exampleSentences: The pub-sub model keeps producers completely independent of consumers.
The pub-sub model scales the producer side without touching it.
In a pub-sub model a slow subscriber is a problem only for itself.
We use the pub-sub model for domain events and point-to-point for work queues.

defCn: 推送模型：broker 主动把消息推送给消费者。
defEn: A delivery model in which the broker pushes messages to the consumer.
codeExample: prefetch = 100   # broker pushes up to 100 unacked messages
exampleSentence: The push model lowers latency but the broker must buffer for slow consumers.
exampleSentences: The push model lowers latency but the broker must buffer for slow consumers.
The push model delivers messages with less latency than polling.
A push model needs a prefetch limit to protect the consumer.
We moved from a pull model to a push model for the realtime feed.

defCn: 拉取模型：消费者主动从 broker 拉取自己需要的消息。
defEn: A delivery model in which consumers fetch the messages they are ready to handle.
exampleSentence: The pull model gives the consumer full control over its own pace.
exampleSentences: The pull model gives the consumer full control over its own pace.
The pull model avoids buffering messages for a slow consumer.
Our pull model checks the queue length before issuing a fetch.
The pull model pairs naturally with a batch size limit.

defCn: 主题通配符：用 * 与 # 匹配一类路由键的规则。
defEn: A pattern that matches a family of routing keys instead of one exact key.
codeExample:
binding routing_key = 'order.*'   # '*' matches one word
binding routing_key = 'order.#'   # '#' matches many
exampleSentence: The topic wildcard lets one subscriber receive a whole family of events.
exampleSentences: The topic wildcard lets one subscriber receive a whole family of events.
Using a topic wildcard is convenient but it hides unintended subscriptions.
We review every topic wildcard binding during the monthly audit.
The hash wildcard matches zero or more words in the routing key.

defCn: 持久队列：broker 重启后仍保留消息的队列类型。
defEn: A queue whose messages survive a broker restart.
exampleSentence: The durable queue keeps the billing messages safe across a broker restart.
exampleSentences: The durable queue keeps the billing messages safe across a broker restart.
A durable queue needs persistent messages to be useful.
Switching to a durable queue was mandatory for the payment flow.
The durable queue costs some throughput because messages are written to disk.

defCn: 会话超时：broker 判定消费者失联并重新分配分区的等待时间。
defEn: How long the broker waits before declaring a consumer dead and reassigning its partitions.
exampleSentence: A long session timeout avoids rebalances but slows the recovery of a dead consumer.
exampleSentences: A long session timeout avoids rebalances but slows the recovery of a dead consumer.
The session timeout must be several times the heartbeat interval.
We lowered the session timeout so a crashed consumer is detected quickly.
A session timeout that is too short causes constant group rebalances.

defCn: 批等待时间：生产者在发送前为凑批最多等待的时长。
defEn: The maximum time a producer waits to accumulate more records into one batch.
codeExample: linger.ms = 5   # wait up to 5ms to fill a batch
exampleSentence: A longer linger improves batching but adds a small delay to every message.
exampleSentences: A longer linger improves batching but adds a small delay to every message.
We set linger to five milliseconds to balance throughput against latency.
Setting linger to zero sends each record immediately at a cost in throughput.
The linger setting is one of the biggest levers on producer performance.

defCn: 滑动跳跃窗口：每次窗口向前移动固定步长且相互重叠的窗口类型。
defEn: A window type that advances by a fixed step while overlapping the previous window.
exampleSentence: The hopping window computes a smooth moving average over the last minute.
exampleSentences: The hopping window computes a smooth moving average over the last minute.
A hopping window gives a continuous result where a tumbling window gives steps.
We use a hopping window for the real time traffic chart.
Overlapping windows cost more because each record is counted several times.

defCn: 水位线：流处理中表示事件时间进度的标记。
defEn: A marker in a stream that shows how far event time has progressed.
exampleSentence: The watermark tells the engine when it is safe to close a window.
exampleSentences: The watermark tells the engine when it is safe to close a window.
A watermark that advances too slowly keeps windows open forever.
We set the watermark to tolerate two minutes of out of order events.
Once the watermark passes the window end, the result is emitted.

defCn: 会话窗口：按不活跃间隔把事件切分成一段段会话的窗口。
defEn: A window that groups events into sessions separated by a period of inactivity.
exampleSentence: The session window counts one visit per user regardless of event spacing.
exampleSentences: The session window counts one visit per user regardless of event spacing.
A session window is the right shape for per visit analytics.
The session window merges events until the gap threshold is exceeded.
We use a session window to compute visits from raw page events.

defCn: 迟到事件：其事件时间早于已关闭窗口的晚到数据。
defEn: A record that arrives after the window it belongs to has already been closed.
exampleSentence: A late event would normally be dropped, so we send it to a side stream.
exampleSentences: A late event would normally be dropped, so we send it to a side stream.
Late events are the main reason we keep an allowed lateness window.
The late event count is a good indicator of upstream clock problems.
We store late events for one day so they can be reprocessed.

defCn: 事件时间：事件实际发生的时间，通常记录在负载之中。
defEn: The time an event actually happened, usually carried inside its payload.
exampleSentence: Event time gives correct results even when events arrive out of order.
exampleSentences: Event time gives correct results even when events arrive out of order.
Using event time makes the pipeline independent of arrival order.
The event time comes from the business system, not from the broker.
We log the difference between event time and processing time to detect skew.

defCn: 处理时间：引擎实际处理这条记录的时刻。
defEn: The moment the engine actually handles a record.
exampleSentence: The gap between processing time and event time is our end to end lag.
exampleSentences: The gap between processing time and event time is our end to end lag.
Processing time is easy to observe but it hides the real order of events.
A long processing time delay means the pipeline is falling behind.
We track processing time separately for each stage of the job.

defCn: 允许迟到时间：窗口关闭后仍接受迟到数据的宽限期。
defEn: The grace period during which a closed window still accepts late records.
codeExample:
allowed_lateness = 30s
# window fires early, then updates again
exampleSentence: Allowed lateness trades a small amount of extra state for fewer dropped records.
exampleSentences: Allowed lateness trades a small amount of extra state for fewer dropped records.
We set an allowed lateness of thirty seconds for the reporting windows.
Too much allowed lateness keeps state around and slows the job.
The allowed lateness value must match the real disorder in your stream.

defCn: 状态后端：流处理引擎保存算子状态与检查点的存储系统。
defEn: The storage system where a stream engine keeps operator state and checkpoints.
exampleSentence: The state backend is what allows the job to resume after a failure.
exampleSentences: The state backend is what allows the job to resume after a failure.
A slow state backend was the real bottleneck of our streaming job.
The state backend stores keyed state per partition.
We moved the state backend to a local disk to cut checkpoint time.

defCn: 输出连接器：把流式结果写入外部系统（如数据库或对象存储）的组件。
defEn: A component that writes streaming results out to an external system.
exampleSentence: The sink connector handles the delivery guarantees of writing to the database.
exampleSentences: The sink connector handles the delivery guarantees of writing to the database.
The sink connector retries writes with exponential backoff.
Our sink connector batches rows before committing them.
Choosing a sink connector that supports exactly-once writes saved us a lot of work.

defCn: 输入连接器：从外部系统读取数据并转成流记录的组件。
defEn: A component that reads from an external system and turns the data into stream records.
exampleSentence: The source connector keeps the offset of the last read record.
exampleSentences: The source connector keeps the offset of the last read record.
Our source connector reads changes and emits them as events.
A source connector must remember its position so it can resume cleanly.
The source connector emits a tombstone record when a row is deleted.

defCn: 租户隔离：保证一个租户的数据与负载不会影响其他租户。
defEn: Guarantees that one tenant's data and load cannot affect any other tenant.
exampleSentence: Tenant isolation is enforced at the query layer, not in application code.
exampleSentences: Tenant isolation is enforced at the query layer, not in application code.
Row level security gives us tenant isolation without changing every query.
A noisy tenant must not break tenant isolation for the others.
We test tenant isolation with a dedicated security test suite.

defCn: 多租户：同一套系统与代码同时服务多个相互隔离的客户。
defEn: Serving many separate customers from one deployment with logical separation.
exampleSentence: Multi-tenancy amortises the platform cost across every customer.
exampleSentences: Multi-tenancy amortises the platform cost across every customer.
Multi-tenancy is much cheaper than running one deployment per customer.
The hard part of multi-tenancy is making noisy neighbours behave.
We chose multi-tenancy over single tenancy for the self service tier.

defCn: 渐进式发布：逐步把新版本放量给用户并观察指标。
defEn: Releasing a new version to users in increasing steps while watching the metrics.
exampleSentence: Progressive delivery turns a risky release into a series of small experiments.
exampleSentences: Progressive delivery turns a risky release into a series of small experiments.
Progressive delivery with automatic gates caught the regression at one percent.
The team adopted progressive delivery after a bad launch.
Each progressive delivery step needs a clear rollback signal.

defCn: 线性一致性：每个操作看起来都在某个瞬间原子生效的强一致模型。
defEn: A consistency model where every operation appears to take effect atomically at some point.
codeExample:
lock = read_write_lock()
with lock: value = compute()
exampleSentence: A linearizable registry guarantees the leader is unique at any instant.
exampleSentences: A linearizable registry guarantees the leader is unique at any instant.
Linearizability is what lets a leader election be safe.
The cache in front of it breaks linearizability unless it is invalidated.
Providing linearizability usually costs an extra round trip per operation.

defCn: 顺序一致性：所有进程看到相同顺序的操作，但不要求符合真实时间。
defEn: A model where all processes see operations in the same order, without real time constraints.
codeExample:
# every replica applies the log in the same order
replicas.forEach(r => r.apply(entry))
exampleSentence: Sequential consistency is enough for a replicated state machine.
exampleSentences: Sequential consistency is enough for a replicated state machine.
Sequential consistency keeps a single logical history across all replicas.
The log ordering gives us sequential consistency for free.
Real time ordering would demand linearizability instead.

defCn: 可串行化：并发事务的效果等同于某个串行顺序执行的结果。
defEn: The property that concurrent transactions behave as if run one after another.
exampleSentence: Serializability is the strongest isolation level for relational databases.
exampleSentences: Serializability is the strongest isolation level for relational databases.
The transfer needs serializability or the balance can go negative.
We chose serializability for the ledger and accepted the retry rate.
Serializability is often implemented with optimistic concurrency checks.

defCn: 因果一致性：保证有因果关系的操作在所有副本上顺序可见。
defEn: A model that preserves the order of causally related operations across replicas.
exampleSentence: Causal consistency keeps the reply after the question without a global lock.
exampleSentences: Causal consistency keeps the reply after the question without a global lock.
Causal consistency is a good fit for collaborative editing.
The version vector carries the causal information needed for this model.
Stronger than eventual, weaker than linearizable, causal consistency is a practical middle ground.

defCn: 读己之写：保证用户写完后立即能读到自己的更新。
defEn: The guarantee that a client sees its own writes after they complete.
exampleSentence: Read-your-writes consistency removes the confusing empty page after a save.
exampleSentences: Read-your-writes consistency removes the confusing empty page after a save.
The cart page needs read-your-writes or users see a stale basket.
We implement read-your-writes by pinning the read to the primary.
A replica lag breaks read-your-writes unless the client waits for the offset.

defCn: 单调读：保证同一客户端后续读到的数据不会比之前更旧。
defEn: The guarantee that a client's later reads never return older data than earlier reads.
exampleSentence: Monotonic read stops a user from seeing an old value after a new one.
exampleSentences: Monotonic read stops a user from seeing an old value after a new one.
Monotonic read is enough for most user facing list pages.
We track the last seen version to enforce monotonic read on replicas.
Monotonic read is weaker than read-your-writes and much cheaper.

defCn: 一致性模型：描述系统在并发读写下对外表现的一组语义契约。
defEn: A named contract describing how a system behaves under concurrent reads and writes.
exampleSentence: Pick the consistency model before picking the database, not after.
exampleSentences: Pick the consistency model before picking the database, not after.
The consistency model is part of the service contract with the caller.
We document the consistency model in the API reference for every endpoint.
Changing the consistency model late is extremely expensive.

defCn: 先行后继关系：定义两个事件之间因果先后顺序的关系。
defEn: The relation that defines which event must be observed before another one.
codeExample:
if write(x) happens-before read(x): return new_value
else: return maybe_old
exampleSentence: The happens-before relation is the backbone of every consistency argument.
exampleSentences: The happens-before relation is the backbone of every consistency argument.
Program order and synchronization order both create happens-before edges.
A race exists only when two events are unordered under happens-before.
Lock acquisition creates a happens-before edge between the critical sections.

defCn: 逻辑时钟：用计数而非物理时间刻画事件先后关系的时钟。
defEn: A counter that captures the causal order of events without relying on wall clock time.
exampleSentence: A logical clock gives a total order without trusting synchronised hardware clocks.
exampleSentences: A logical clock gives a total order without trusting synchronised hardware clocks.
The logical clock increments on every local event and on every message receive.
Because the logical clock is monotone, message order can be reconstructed.
We use a logical clock for the audit trail in the payment service.

defCn: Lamport 时间戳：为事件分配的满足因果顺序的逻辑时间标记。
defEn: A logical timestamp that respects the causal ordering of distributed events.
codeExample:
on_send: ts = max(ts, last_seen) + 1
on_receive: last_seen = max(last_seen, msg.ts)
exampleSentence: Lamport timestamps let us detect whether two events really are concurrent.
exampleSentences: Lamport timestamps let us detect whether two events really are concurrent.
The Lamport timestamp is only meaningful together with the process id.
We use Lamport timestamps to order the audit events of a distributed transaction.
A Lamport timestamp guarantees order but not real time ordering.

defCn: 混合逻辑时钟：把物理时间与逻辑计数结合的时间戳方案。
defEn: A timestamp scheme that combines physical time with a logical counter.
codeExample:
now = max(physical_now, last.hlc) + 1
if physical_now - last.wall > drift: bump_logical()
exampleSentence: A hybrid logical clock keeps timestamps close to real time while staying monotonic.
exampleSentences: A hybrid logical clock keeps timestamps close to real time while staying monotonic.
The hybrid logical clock survives clock adjustments on one machine.
We chose a hybrid logical clock for the multi region database.
Compared with a pure logical clock, the hybrid version stays human readable.

defCn: 向量时钟：记录各节点计数以检测并发更新的时钟结构。
defEn: A clock structure that tracks a counter per node so concurrency can be detected.
codeExample:
vc = {'a': 3, 'b': 1}
merge = {k: max(vc[k], other[k]) for k in set(vc) | set(other)}
exampleSentence: A vector clock can tell two concurrent updates apart from a simple ordering.
exampleSentences: A vector clock can tell two concurrent updates apart from a simple ordering.
The vector clock grows with the number of nodes but stays small in practice.
We compare vector clocks to decide whether a conflict needs manual resolution.
Vector clocks are the classic alternative to physical clock synchronisation.

defCn: 版本向量：记录各副本写入版本以判断数据新旧的结构。
defEn: A structure that stores the version of each replica to compare data freshness.
exampleSentence: The version vector tells the writer which replica already has the newest data.
exampleSentences: The version vector tells the writer which replica already has the newest data.
A version vector is a practical way to implement read repair.
Comparing version vectors is how we detect which copy is stale.
The version vector adds a small metadata header to every write.

defCn: 反熵：节点间周期性比对状态以修复数据差异的机制。
defEn: A background process that periodically compares replicas and repairs differences.
codeExample:
hinted_handoff_queue = reconcile(nodes)
for node in nodes: sync_digest(node)
exampleSentence: Anti-entropy keeps replicas converged after a network partition heals.
exampleSentences: Anti-entropy keeps replicas converged after a network partition heals.
Anti-entropy turned a rare data divergence into a self healing condition.
The anti-entropy run compares checksums rather than full rows.
Without anti-entropy, two replicas can stay different for months.

defCn: 提示转交：目标节点不可用时由他人暂存数据并稍后投递。
defEn: Storing a write on another node when the target is down and delivering it later.
exampleSentence: Hinted handoff keeps writes available while one replica is down.
exampleSentences: Hinted handoff keeps writes available while one replica is down.
The hinted handoff queue must expire hints so they do not resurrect old data.
Hinted handoff is what allows an update to succeed with a quorum of replicas.
We monitor the size of the hinted handoff queue as a health signal.

defCn: 读修复：读取时发现副本数据不一致就顺手修复其他副本。
defEn: Fixing stale replicas opportunistically when a read reveals a divergence.
codeExample:
value, stale = quorum_read(key)
if stale: async_write(stale_replicas, value)
exampleSentence: Read repair quietly fixes divergence without a separate repair job.
exampleSentences: Read repair quietly fixes divergence without a separate repair job.
Read repair only works when a quorum of replicas disagree clearly.
The repair must be asynchronous so the read path stays fast.
Read repair is cheap to add and removes most stale read complaints.

defCn: 宽松仲裁：允许用任意副本集合凑够数量但牺牲一致性保证。
defEn: A quorum mode that accepts any set of replicas at the cost of stronger guarantees.
codeExample:
quorum = 'sloppy'
# write to the first N replicas that respond, not a fixed set
exampleSentence: A sloppy quorum keeps writes available when the preferred replica is down.
exampleSentences: A sloppy quorum keeps writes available when the preferred replica is down.
The sloppy quorum mode trades consistency for availability during a failure.
We only enable a sloppy quorum for hints, never for real writes.
Turning off sloppy quorum made the behaviour predictable again.

defCn: 租约过期：持有者失联后锁或领导权自动释放的时间界限。
defEn: The deadline after which an unreachable lease holder loses its claim.
exampleSentence: Lease expiry is how a leader lock recovers from a crashed holder.
exampleSentences: Lease expiry is how a leader lock recovers from a crashed holder.
A lease that is too short causes needless leader churn.
The lease expiry must be longer than the worst case pause.
We use lease expiry with a fencing token to stop a zombie leader.

defCn: 栅栏令牌：单调递增的编号，用于拒绝过期持有者的写入。
defEn: A monotonically increasing number that lets the resource reject stale writers.
exampleSentence: The fencing token makes it safe to use a lock when the holder may be paused.
exampleSentences: The fencing token makes it safe to use a lock when the holder may be paused.
A fencing token protects the storage from a partitioned old leader.
The resource compares the fencing token and rejects anything older.
We added a fencing token after a split brain wrote twice.

defCn: 状态机复制：让所有副本按相同日志顺序执行相同状态转移。
defEn: Replicating a log so every replica applies the same state transitions in the same order.
codeExample:
for entry in committed_log:
    state = apply(state, entry.command)
exampleSentence: State machine replication is the foundation of Raft and etcd.
exampleSentences: State machine replication is the foundation of Raft and etcd.
The state machine replication model keeps every replica byte identical.
A snapshot lets a lagging replica catch up in state machine replication.
Deterministic commands are required for state machine replication to work.

defCn: 提交索引：领导者已复制并可安全应用的日志位置。
defEn: The position in the log that the leader knows is replicated safely.
codeExample: commit_index = min(index of last entry in each in-sync replica)
exampleSentence: The commit index tells the leader which entries it may apply locally.
exampleSentences: The commit index tells the leader which entries it may apply locally.
The commit index only advances when a quorum has stored the entry.

defCn: 扩展收缩法：先兼容新旧结构再回填最后删除旧字段的迁移方法。

defCn: 变更流：按顺序输出数据库所有变更的连续事件序列。

defCn: 事件流：按发生顺序排列、只追加不修改的事件序列。

defCn: 事件重放：重新消费历史事件以重建状态或复现问题。

defCn: 读模型：为查询场景预先计算好的专用数据视图。
